findings.message: AC-2 moved the in-force reads to each person's own today, but only where no date is passed. The screens still pass UTC's today. PeoplePage still computes `on = todayIso()` (UTC) and passes it to `peopleStats` (stats.ts:16, and its `employmentAt(now)` at stats.ts:23) and to `<Directory today={on}>`. The directory beside them now reads each person's local date. PersonPage.tsx:20 passes `today()` (UTC) to `getPersonView`, so the person view's directory row and its `getEmployment` still read UTC's date, and `statusChip(p, on)` does too. T3 names the person view as in scope. Fix: stop passing UTC's today to these reads, or take the date from the same per-entity rule, and remove `today` from inforce.ts once nothing uses it. Add the People stats and the person page to the AC-2 variant test.
findings.scenario: At 2026-11-15T20:00Z (already the 16th in Colombo), HR changes an LK engineer's department to Quality with no date. The change takes effect 2026-11-16. The directory row shows Quality. 'People by department' on the same screen still counts them under the old department, and their person page (/hr/LL-xxxx) still shows the old department and employment period until 00:00 UTC.

findings.message: AC-3 says the attention line's pin is 'on the entity', and core rule 2 says a pin resolves through a read tool to that exact record. Here an admin gets `list_schedules` (a view of every schedule) and anyone else gets `people_stats`, which says nothing about time zones. Both carry a label made from the entity's name. Neither resolves to the entity or its missing zone, so pinning 'Lumen Labs Pty Ltd: no time zone' gives chat unrelated data, and the Ask amax prompt to set the zone goes out pinned to it. Fix: pin to a read tool keyed by the entity's id (`pin: { id, of }`) that returns the entity and its zone status. If no such tool exists, add one. Read the label from the record.
findings.scenario: A non-admin HR user pins 'Lumen Labs Pty Ltd: no time zone' and asks chat why. The pin resolves to `people_stats` (headcount, joiners, probation), which has no zone or entity data, so chat can't answer about the pinned item.

findings.message: Before this diff, the audited system read of unmasked pay and bank data recorded the as-of date it read. Now `on` defaults to undefined, the date is worked out inside SQL by `localToday()`, and the audit stores `on: null`. The persisted audit row no longer says which employment period was read. Fix: select the resolved as-of date as a column (for example `asOf(on) as as_of`) and audit that value.
findings.scenario: At 2026-11-15T20:00Z a payroll job calls `getEmployment(tx, lkPersonId, systemCtx)`. The person has a pay rise starting 2026-11-16. The job gets the new salary (local date: 16th), but the audit says `{ on: null }`. An auditor can't tell whether the old or the new salary period was disclosed.

findings.message: `localToday()` copies `entityZoneSet`'s zone lookup (the entity's own zone, else `ENTITY_ZONES[trim(country)]`) into SQL. That is why `ENTITY_ZONES` is now exported from the `@amax/workflows` root (packages/workflows/src/index.ts:3), a platform-package edit that isn't in the plan's file list. `unzonedEntities` (zones.ts:22) also repeats `applyStatusDates`' per-entity `entityZoneSet` loop (services.ts:130–134): the page and the job each work out the unzoned list on their own. Keep one copy of the zone resolution in @amax/workflows (a SQL expression or function it exports), and have the job report `unzonedEntities`' result.

For an entity with no time zone, in-force reads quietly use UTC's date. Contract readers (`getPerson`, `listPeople`, `getEmployment`, `reportUserIds`) get no sign that the date is a fallback. 109 said such an entity is 'never counted in UTC', and only the People screen flags it. At least mark the result, or document in contracts.ts that the date falls back to UTC for these readers.

The `allocations.standing for ${updated_by}` attribution is now written twice in the same loop (lines 49 and 57). Work out `by` once per row before the branch, and use it for both the end and the extension.

AC-2's variant table covers `getPerson`, `listPeople` and `getEmployment`. It doesn't cover `reportUserIds` or `personByNo` (the write scope's department), even though both changed to the local date in this diff. AC-1 has no case where a person field with `effectiveOn` set to UTC's date (2026-11-15) is refused at 20:00Z, which is the other half of the changed `on !== local` check.

AC-2 makes HR's in-force reads default to each person's own today, but this diff updates only the callers that left `on` empty. These callers still pass UTC `today()` explicitly: PersonPage (`const on = today()` → `getPersonView(viewer, …, on)` and `statusChip(p, on)`), PeoplePage (`const on = todayIso()` → `peopleStats(viewer, on, …)`) and `peopleStats`' own default (`stats.ts:16`, `asOf = todayIso()` → `employmentAt(now)` for the department chart). So the person screen, the stats and the people_stats MCP tool still use the UTC day. The directory row on the same People page now uses the local day, so the page shows two different days. Fix: drop the explicit UTC date from these callers so they get the per-person local default, and remove `peopleStats`' UTC default. Add these readers to the AC-2 variant test.
findings.scenario: At 2026-11-15T20:00Z, change_person sets department 'Quality' for a Sri Lanka person, effective the local today 2026-11-16. The directory and get_person show 'Quality'. /hr/<employeeNo> (PersonPage reads on 2026-11-15) still shows the old department, and the People page's department chart (peopleStats on 2026-11-15) still counts them in the old department.

findings.message: The 'no time zone' test deletes Australia's zone and restores it only after the assertion. If the assertion fails, the zone stays deleted and the later tests in the file that share this database break. Restore it in try/finally or afterEach. unzoned-110.test.ts has the same problem: its job test leaves the zone deleted.
